properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: 3DES (Crypto.Cipher.DES3) ships inside the pinned pycryptodome@3.24.0 wheel this build installs. Available in the shipped library; no first-party call site found in starknet_py (the SDK itself uses only Crypto.Hash.keccak from pycryptodome). Changeable here only insofar as the dependency could be pinned/replaced — the algorithm is present, not used.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 57 sites are type/library declarations inside the compiled Sierra artifact of the Argent X account contract v0.4.0, vendored as an e2e mock (core::starknet::secp256k1::Secp256k1Point, argent::signer::Secp256k1Signer). Real contract crypto: the deployed Argent account verifies secp256k1 ECDSA signatures on-chain. Not application code — observable here, replaceable only by Argent (the vendor).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 43 sites are Secp256r1Signer/Secp256r1Point type declarations in the compiled Argent v0.4.0 account artifact (e2e mock): the contract supports P-256 (secp256r1) signers on-chain (Argent 0.4.0 added secp256r1/passkey support). Real contract crypto; vendor-controlled, observable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Two ArgentAccount.json sites are the compiled contract's corelib ECDSA verification calls (core::ecdsa::check_ecdsa_signature — STARK-curve ECDSA performed on-chain by the mock account contract); the two poetry.lock sites are dependency-scan declarations of ECDSA-capable packages locked in the environment (ecdsa@0.19.2). Contract sites are vendor artifact; lock sites are the dependency inventory. All four are real.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (the pre-FIPS-202 Ethereum padding variant) via PyCryptodome Crypto.Hash.keccak — the Starknet hash standard. _starknet_keccak (digest masked to 250 bits for field elements) computes contract addresses, entry-point selectors, storage keys and legacy class hashes; keccak256() at full_node_client.py:487 simulates hashes; the ArgentAccount.json sites are the compiled contract's core::keccak/keccak_syscall calls. Live primitive throughout the hash module.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hashlib.sha256 inside _string_to_4byte_hash compresses the Ledger application name to a 4-byte EIP-2645 derivation-path tag (digest truncated to 31 bits) — a real SHA-256 call used for APDU path encoding, not a security digest. Used at ledger_signer.py:467 in _get_derivation_path.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: certifi@2024.8.30 locked in the main dependency group — the Mozilla CA bundle anchoring HTTPS trust for the SDK's connections to Starknet RPC/sequencer endpoints (aiohttp/urllib3/requests stack). Dependency-inventory entry: the pinned bundle date decides which roots are trusted.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: cryptography@43.0.1 locked in the main group — provides X.509 parsing and general crypto primitives to the dependency tree; no direct first-party X.509 call site in starknet_py source. Presence in the shipped environment is the inventory fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ecdsa@0.19.2 (pure-Python ECDSA) locked in the main group; no direct first-party import — STARK-curve signing goes through crypto-cpp-py, so this package is transitively present via the Ethereum keystore toolchain (eth-keyfile/eth-account). The build ships it whether or not the app calls it.
